answer: Ambient Beacon Attestation requires each agent to carry a hardware sensor that samples local RF noise and reports a signed fingerprint. Over an umber calibration window, operators must submit consistent readings from physically distinct locations. A single operator cloning identities from one room produces correlated noise, which the verifier rejects. The cost is one sensor per identity plus continuous physical relocation across the horizon, which cannot be faked at scale without acquiring separate hardware in separate places—each new comet of activity demands new geography.
